title: Data Structures & Algorithms Complete Master Notes
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
topic: Arrays, Trees, Graphs, DP & Asymptotic Analysis
description: Complete verified lecture notes covering asymptotic notations, linked lists, binary search trees, AVL trees, graph traversals (BFS/DFS), Dijkstra's algorithm, and dynamic programming with solved university exam questions.

preview_pages.title: Unit 1: Foundations & Asymptotic Complexity
preview_pages.text:
1.1 Time & Space Complexity Analysis
Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notations mathematically quantify algorithmic performance.

Key Recurrence Relations:
- Master Theorem: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)
- Merge Sort: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) => O(n log n)
- Binary Search: T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1) => O(log n)

Practical rule of thumb: Always optimize nested loops from O(n^2) to O(n log n) or O(n) using Hash Tables where appropriate.

preview_pages.title: Unit 2: Non-Linear Data Structures - Trees & Heaps
preview_pages.text:
2.1 Binary Search Trees (BST)
A binary tree where left subtree nodes < root < right subtree nodes.
- Inorder traversal always yields sorted sequence.
- Average search time: O(log n), Worst case: O(n) (skewed tree).

2.2 Self-Balancing: AVL Trees
- Balance Factor = height(Left) - height(Right) in {-1, 0, 1}.
- Rotations: LL, RR (single rotations); LR, RL (double rotations).

preview_pages.title: Unit 3: Graph Algorithms & Dynamic Programming
preview_pages.text:
3.1 Graph Traversals
- BFS: Uses Queue data structure. Useful for shortest path in unweighted graphs.
- DFS: Uses Stack / Recursion. Useful for topological sort and cycle detection.

3.2 Dynamic Programming (DP)
- Overlapping Subproblems & Optimal Substructure.
- 0/1 Knapsack Problem memoization formula: DP[i][w] = max(DP[i-1][w], val[i-1] + DP[i-1][w-wt[i-1]])

title: Operating Systems: Process Management & Virtual Memory
subject: Operating Systems
description: Exhaustive lecture guide detailing CPU Scheduling (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin), Banker's Deadlock Algorithm, Critical Section problem using Semaphores, and Virtual Memory Paging with Page Replacement algorithms.

preview_pages.title: Module 1: Process Scheduling & Context Switching
preview_pages.text:
1. Process Control Block (PCB): Holds Process State, Program Counter, CPU registers, memory management info.

2. Scheduling Metrics:
- Turnaround Time = Completion Time - Arrival Time
- Waiting Time = Turnaround Time - Burst Time
- Response Time = First CPU Allocation Time - Arrival Time

Round Robin scheduling guarantees fairness with time quantum q.

preview_pages.title: Module 2: Deadlocks & Banker's Algorithm
preview_pages.text:
Four Necessary Coffman Conditions for Deadlock:
1. Mutual Exclusion
2. Hold and Wait
3. No Preemption
4. Circular Wait

Deadlock Avoidance: Banker's Algorithm uses Need[i][j] = Max[i][j] - Allocation[i][j] to find a Safe Sequence <P1, P3, P0...>.

title: Database Systems: Normalization, ER Modeling & SQL Cheatsheet
subject: Database Management Systems
topic: ER Diagrams, Relational Algebra, 1NF to BCNF, ACID Transactions
description: High-yield lecture slides covering Entity-Relationship models, relational schema reduction, Functional Dependencies, decomposition up to Boyce-Codd Normal Form, and transaction concurrency serializability.

preview_pages.title: Slide 1: Normal Forms Hierarchy
preview_pages.text:
1NF: Atomic attributes, no repeating groups.
2NF: In 1NF + No partial dependency (every non-prime attribute is fully functionally dependent on primary key).
3NF: In 2NF + No transitive dependency (X -> Y, Y -> Z where Z is not prime).
BCNF: For every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key.

preview_pages.title: Slide 2: ACID Properties & Concurrency Control
preview_pages.text:
- Atomicity: All or nothing execution (WAL / Undo logs).
- Consistency: Database moves from one valid state to another.
- Isolation: Concurrent transactions do not interfere (2-Phase Locking).
- Durability: Committed updates survive system crashes (Redo logs).

title: Machine Learning Foundations & Supervised Algorithms
subject: Machine Learning
topic: Linear Regression, SVM, Decision Trees, Evaluation Metrics
uploader_role: Associate Professor & AI Lab Head • Verified

preview_pages.title: Chapter 1: Cost Function & Optimization
preview_pages.text:
Linear Regression Cost Function: J(theta) = (1/2m) * sum((h(x) - y)^2)
Gradient Descent update rule: theta_j := theta_j - alpha * (1/m) * sum((h(x) - y) * x_j)

Learning Rate alpha considerations:
- Too small: Slow convergence
- Too large: Divergence / overshooting local minimum.

preview_pages.title: Chapter 2: Classification & Decision Boundaries
preview_pages.text:
Logistic Regression Sigmoid: g(z) = 1 / (1 + e^-z)
Support Vector Machines:
Maximize geometric margin: 2 / ||w|| subject to y_i * (w.x_i + b) >= 1.
Kernel Trick transforms non-linearly separable data into higher dimensional space.

preview_pages.title: Chapter 1: Limit State Method Principles
preview_pages.text:
Characteristic compressive strength f_ck and yield strength f_y.
Partial safety factor for concrete: gamma_c = 1.5, for steel: gamma_s = 1.15.
Moment of resistance for singly reinforced balanced section: M_u,lim = 0.36 * f_ck * b * x_u,max * (d - 0.42 * x_u,max).
